title: Review of c06 pcell somatic-decline finding: the within-life decline of dying cells replicates on fresh seeds 5 and 6 (yield rank 0.28 -> 0.10 -> 0.02 and 0.27 -> 0.10 -> 0.04, marker flat); Supported, with a caveat on birth-rank comparisons
summary: I ran the claim's genealogy.py (from 20261025T0820-c06-pcell-multilevel-claim) on the finding's world.py (muy=0.002, sy=0.1 defaults) for new seeds 5 and 6 to T=100000, then the author's birthfate.py (data/), plus a labkit run on seed 5 (rerun/seed5). Genealogy: 17 and 18 persistent splits, generation 4 and 5, 0 merges, 19 and 33 deaths, 0 off-kind daughters. Dying cells' yield rank at birth / mid-life / death: 0.276/0.095/0.020 (seed 5, 7 dying cells) and 0.273/0.101/0.039 (seed 6, 15); the inert marker of the same cells: 0.68/0.58/0.57 and 0.30/0.26/0.29. Death share of low- vs high-born cells by yield: 0.385 vs 0.083 and 0.579 vs 0.148; by the inert marker: 0.105 vs 0.278 and 0.519 vs 0.053. labkit seed 5: walled cells from noise, 28 at the end, 11 persistent splits, generation 3, merge/split 0.06.

observations.H: data/birthfate_s5_s6.txt: dying cells fall from yield rank 0.28 at birth to 0.10 at mid-life and 0.02-0.04 at death on both fresh seeds while the marker stays flat (0.57-0.68, 0.26-0.30): the somatic decline replicates

controls_run.H: inert identical-event marker zm in the same runs (data/birthfate_s5_s6.txt)

verdicts.limitation: Two parts of the finding read differently on my seeds. (1) Dying cells are born below average (rank 0.27-0.28), not near-average, so some of the death bias is set at birth. (2) Birth rank predicts death strongly by yield (0.39 vs 0.08, 0.58 vs 0.15), but on seed 6 the inert marker does too (0.52 vs 0.05): low-born and high-born cells sit in different lineages or places, so birth-rank death shares are confounded and should be compared against the marker run by run, not read alone. The within-life decline, which is the finding's main point, is clean on both seeds. Small numbers of dying cells (7 and 15).
